chunks: From him, from one of our companions, from Mubarak, the slave of Al-Aqarquqi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Habitual wearing of the socks is a security from the tuberculosis.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of wearing socks (khuff) during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the habitual wearing of leather socks (khuff) to protection from 'al-sill,' which classical Shia exegetes often interpret as tuberculosis or a general respiratory weakness, reflecting the medical understanding of the era. This narration highlights the intersection of ritual purity mechanics and physical health in Shia jurisprudence, suggesting that consistent adherence to this specific garment fosters bodily resilience.

en.hubeali:
From him, from one of our companions, from Mubarak a slave of Al Aqarquqy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Habitual wearing of the socks is a security from the tuberculosis’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain persons of our people from Mubarak Ghulam al-‘Aqarqufiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Continuously wearing al-Khuff (half-boot) provides immunity against tuberculoses.’”
